questions.q: What is the first step of this authorized assessment, before any testing begins?
options: Confirm written scope and rules of engagement for the staging assessment
Immediately submit a destructive payload to production
Disable the retriever entirely for the duration of the test
Skip authorization since staging data isn't real customer data
questions.explain: Rules of engagement -- scope, boundaries, and sign-off -- are what make this an authorized security assessment rather than unapproved probing.

questions.q: Why is past ticket text marked 'untrusted' in the retrieval pipeline map, while help-center articles are marked 'trusted'?
options: Ticket text is encrypted and articles are not
Articles are written by Larkspur's own content team, while ticket text can be written freely by any customer
Ticket text is never actually retrieved by SupportPilot
Trust level is assigned randomly for testing purposes
questions.explain: The source an outside party can freely write to is the one that matters for indirect prompt injection risk -- that's past ticket text here.

questions.q: What makes the Step 4 marker string ('RTX-MARKER-0417') a safe way to test for injection susceptibility?
options: It asks the model to exfiltrate real customer data as proof
It instructs the model to call a destructive tool directly
It only asks for a visible, measurable token to appear in the answer -- it requests nothing destructive or harmful
It is identical to a real customer complaint and cannot be distinguished from one
questions.explain: A marker-string test proves whether retrieved content can influence behavior using a harmless, measurable signal instead of a real payload.

questions.q: In Step 5, what does it mean if RTX-MARKER-0417 appears in SupportPilot's answer to an unrelated query?
options: The retrieval pipeline is completely broken and must be rebuilt
The help-center articles have been compromised
Nothing -- the marker appearing is expected and harmless either way
The model followed an instruction that arrived through retrieved content rather than the actual user -- confirmed indirect prompt injection susceptibility
questions.explain: The marker surfacing in an unrelated answer is the measurable signal that retrieved text was treated as an instruction, not just as reference material.

questions.q: Why does Step 6 document a forward-looking finding about tools, even though staging SupportPilot has no tool access yet?
options: Because tool access is irrelevant to this assessment
Because it justifies privilege separation and a gate before any tool gets wired in, rather than discovering the risk only after tools already exist
Because the finding requires actually attaching and triggering a destructive tool to be valid
Because Lesson 30's feature will never need any security review
questions.explain: Flagging the risk before tools are attached is what lets the next lesson's checklist gate the feature before it ships, instead of reacting after an incident.
